//: Realtime Database rules for the 'marioish' project.
or paste into Firebase console > Realtime Database > Rules.
Requires the Anonymous sign-in provider to be enabled under
Authentication > Sign-in method. Without it every client falls back to
single player, because game.js refuses to connect unauthenticated.
Anonymous auth is not a gate on who can play - anyone holding the public
web config can mint a token. It exists so that auth.uid is server-verified,
which lets these rules pin each player to their own node. That stops the
griefing that actually matters in a game like this: editing someone else's
score, impersonating another player, or wiping the world in one write.
The size and shape limits below matter for the same reason - names are
rendered in every other player's leaderboard.

$coin.//: A coin node exists only while the coin is banked. Anyone may claim a free coin or clear an expired one; nobody may overwrite a live claim, which is what stops two players banking the same coin.

enemies.//: Shared world state. Only the elected spawn master writes positions, but the election is client-side so the rules cannot enforce which client that is - any signed-in player may write here.

$victim.//: A per-player inbox. You read your own; anyone may post a claim into yours, and the victim's client decides whether to accept it. Only the victim can clear it.

allTimeLeaderboard.//: Read by the start screen. Written through a transaction that trims to the top 10, so the whole node is rewritten as one value.
allTimeLeaderboard.//indexOn: The start screen reads this with orderByChild('score'); without the index Firebase downloads the whole node and sorts on the client.
